description.en-US:
sloppy lightswitch uwu lies to websites about your light/dark mode setting, so a site can be dark while your system is light, or the other way around uwu ~

three modes, global and per site:

  system - nothing is touched, as if the extension were not installed
  light  - the page is convinced your scheme is light
  dark   - the page is convinced your scheme is dark

pick a global mode in the popup and override it for the site in the current tab. per-site wins. the settings page (add-ons manager > sloppy lightswitch > settings) lists every per-site switch, lets you add and remove them, and has a plain text list you can just type into - one site and one mode per line - for when a popup is not an option, like on firefox for android.

the spoofing runs before any page script, including the anti-flash theme sniffers that decide your colours in the first 20ms, so pages come up in the mode you picked instead of flickering into it. window.matchMedia, css @media (prefers-color-scheme) rules, media="" attributes and the browser's own color-scheme pick for form controls and scrollbars all follow.

nothing is collected, stored remotely, or sent anywhere. your modes sit in your own browser storage.

sloppy edges, honestly: open pages pick up a mode change on their next reload, and a site with a very strict style-src csp can block the cross-origin stylesheet swap.

summary.en-US: flips what sites think your system light/dark setting is uwu ~ globally or per site, before the page can flash
